properties.text: For all blob inputs, bytes_to_bls_field MUST reject any byte sequence whose numeric value is greater than or equal to BLS_MODULUS. Any blob byte segment that is not a valid BLS12-381 scalar field element MUST cause cell_to_coset_evals to abort, preventing invalid field elements from entering the polynomial arithmetic pipeline.

reachability.notes: Attacker submits crafted blob data via a blob-carrying transaction (EIP-4844/EIP-7594) over the P2P network. The blob content is entirely attacker-controlled.

properties.severity_justification: Bypassing field element validation would allow an attacker to inject invalid algebraic elements into the polynomial commitment scheme, corrupting all downstream KZG proofs and breaking data availability guarantees network-wide.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a blob byte sequence that bypasses bytes_to_bls_field validation and produces an invalid field element accepted by the polynomial engine.

properties.text: For all blobs submitted for cell encoding, the assertion len(blob) == BYTES_PER_BLOB MUST hold. Any blob with length not equal to BYTES_PER_BLOB MUST be rejected before any cell computation begins.

reachability.notes: Attacker-controlled blob data enters via blob transactions. A missing or bypassed length check could cause buffer over-read or under-read in field element deserialization.

properties.severity_justification: A blob with incorrect length could cause out-of-bounds reads during BYTES_PER_FIELD_ELEMENT segmentation, potentially crashing the node or producing incorrect polynomial representations.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a blob with non-standard length bypassing the length assertion.

properties.text: The batch verification pairing equation e(LL, LR) == e(RL, [1]) in verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl MUST be sound: for all sets of (commitments, cell_indices, cells, proofs), if the pairing check passes, then each cell is a valid evaluation of the polynomial committed by its corresponding commitment at the specified coset, except with negligible probability.

reachability.notes: An adversary could submit forged cells and proofs via the P2P gossip network for batch verification. A soundness failure would allow invalid data to be accepted as available.

properties.severity_justification: A soundness failure in the pairing check would allow an adversary to forge data availability proofs, undermining the entire data availability sampling scheme and potentially enabling invalid state transitions.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate forged (commitment, cell, proof) tuple that passes batch verification but does not correspond to a valid polynomial evaluation.

properties.text: The Fiat-Shamir challenge r derived by compute_verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_challenge MUST include all verifier-relevant data in the hash input: the domain separator, the degree bound, all commitment bytes, all cell indices, all cell evaluations, and all proof bytes. Omitting or reordering any component MUST change the resulting challenge r.

reachability.notes: An adversary who can influence the Fiat-Shamir challenge by manipulating which data is included in the hash can break the security of the batch verification scheme.

properties.severity_justification: If the Fiat-Shamir hash does not bind to all verifier inputs, an adversary can find related input sets that produce the same challenge, enabling proof substitution attacks that break batch verification soundness.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate two different sets of inputs that produce the same Fiat-Shamir challenge due to incomplete or reorderable hash input.

properties.text: The domain separator RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_DOMAIN used in the Fiat-Shamir hash MUST be unique across all protocols using the same hash function. No other protocol or sub-protocol MUST reuse this domain separator value.

reachability.notes: Cross-protocol replay attacks become possible if domain separators collide between different sub-protocols that use the same hash function.

properties.severity_justification: A domain separator collision would enable cross-protocol replay, allowing an adversary to repurpose valid verification transcripts from one context to forge proofs in another.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must identify another protocol using the same domain separator value.

properties.text: For all inputs to verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch (SG-021), the following validation MUST be enforced: (1) all input lists have matching lengths, (2) each commitment is exactly BYTES_PER_COMMITMENT bytes, (3) each cell_index < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB, (4) each cell is exactly BYTES_PER_CELL bytes, (5) each proof is exactly BYTES_PER_PROOF bytes. Any violation MUST cause the function to return false or raise an error before the pairing check.

reachability.notes: An adversary submits malformed verification requests via the P2P network. Bypassing input validation could lead to out-of-bounds access or incorrect pairing computations.

properties.severity_justification: Missing input validation could cause crashes (DoS) or allow malformed data to reach the pairing check, potentially producing incorrect verification results.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate malformed input that bypasses one or more validation checks and reaches the pairing computation.

properties.text: Data recovery via recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs (SG-024) MUST validate: (1) cell_ids and cells have matching lengths, (2) at least CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB / 2 cells are provided, (3) no duplicate cell indices, (4) cell indices are sorted, (5) all cell indices < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB, (6) all cells have correct byte lengths. Any violation MUST prevent recovery from proceeding.

reachability.notes: An adversary could provide crafted partial cell sets to trigger recovery with invalid inputs, potentially causing incorrect polynomial reconstruction.

properties.severity_justification: Recovery of an incorrect polynomial from adversarial inputs would produce invalid cells and proofs that could propagate through the network, breaking data availability guarantees.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate adversarial cell inputs that bypass validation and cause recovery of an incorrect polynomial.

properties.text: After data recovery via recover_polynomialcoeff (SG-023), the recovered polynomial MUST have degree strictly less than FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB. The high-degree coefficients (indices >= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB) of the recovered polynomial from the extended domain MUST all be zero.

validation_layers: Degree bound check on recovered polynomial
reachability.notes: If mutually inconsistent cells are provided for recovery (from different polynomials), the recovered polynomial may have degree >= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB, indicating data corruption.

properties.severity_justification: A recovered polynomial with incorrect degree would produce cells and proofs that are inconsistent with the original blob commitment, enabling data corruption that propagates through the DA layer.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate cell inputs causing recovery of a polynomial with degree >= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB.

properties.text: Cells recovered and regenerated by recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs MUST pass verification against the original KZG commitment via verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch. The round-trip (blob -> cells -> partial subset -> recovery -> regenerated cells) MUST produce cells verifiable against the original commitment.

reachability.notes: This is an end-to-end correctness property. Failure indicates a bug in recovery, proof generation, or both.

properties.severity_justification: If recovered cells fail verification, nodes cannot restore data availability from partial data, breaking the erasure coding recovery guarantee.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a valid subset of cells that, after recovery and regeneration, produces cells that fail KZG batch verification.

properties.text: The KZG trusted setup parameters (KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL, KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL) MUST be validated against known checksums at load time. The G1 and G2 elements MUST originate from the same ceremony. The structured reference string MUST satisfy the expected algebraic relationships: for all i, KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL[i] = [tau^i] * G1.

reachability.notes: The trusted setup is loaded from a static file at startup. A supply-chain attack on the trusted setup file would compromise all KZG operations, but this is outside the runtime attack surface.

properties.severity_justification: Compromised trusted setup allows forging KZG proofs for arbitrary data, completely breaking data availability guarantees.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Trusted setup integrity is a ceremony-level concern, not a runtime vulnerability.

properties.text: The FFT implementation (SG-003, SG-004) MUST only accept inputs whose length is a power of 2. For all input vectors vals, len(vals) MUST equal 2^k for some non-negative integer k.

reachability.notes: FFT inputs are derived from protocol-defined constants (FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB, CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB) which are all powers of 2. An external attacker cannot directly control FFT input length.

properties.severity_justification: Non-power-of-2 FFT input would produce silently incorrect polynomial transformations, corrupting all downstream proofs.

properties.text: polynomial_eval_to_coeff (SG-007) MUST produce the correct coefficient representation of the input polynomial evaluations via inverse FFT with bit-reversal permutation. The output polynomial degree MUST be less than len(input). Specifically, for input evaluations [f(omega^0), ..., f(omega^(n-1))], the output MUST be coefficients [c_0, ..., c_{n-1}] such that f(x) = sum(c_i * x^i).

reachability.notes: The polynomial engine is an internal component. However, incorrect polynomial coefficients would produce invalid KZG proofs for attacker-controlled blob data.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect inverse FFT would produce wrong polynomial coefficients, causing all KZG proofs for any blob to fail verification at receiving nodes.

properties.text: divide_polynomialcoeff (SG-010) MUST reject division by the zero polynomial. For all inputs where the divisor polynomial b is the zero polynomial, the function MUST raise an error or abort.

reachability.notes: Polynomial division is used during recovery (SG-023). The divisor is derived from the vanishing polynomial which should never be zero for valid cell indices.

properties.severity_justification: Division by zero would cause a runtime crash, but the divisor is derived from protocol constants making this condition unlikely unless there is a bug in vanishing polynomial construction.

properties.text: interpolate_polynomialcoeff (SG-011) MUST receive distinct x-values. For all input sets of (x_values, y_values), all elements in x_values MUST be pairwise distinct. Duplicate x-values MUST cause the function to abort or produce an error.

reachability.notes: Lagrange interpolation x-values are derived from coset evaluation points which are distinct by construction.

properties.severity_justification: Duplicate x-values would cause division by zero in Lagrange basis computation, crashing the node.

properties.text: Validators MUST publish each data column sidecar to the correct gossip subnet determined by compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar(column_index). The subnet assignment MUST be deterministic and consistent across all validators for the same column_index.

reachability.notes: A validator publishing to the wrong subnet would prevent peers from receiving data columns they need for data availability verification. A malicious validator could exploit this to selectively deny data to specific peers.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect subnet routing would cause data columns to be invisible to peers expecting them on the correct subnet, potentially causing data availability failures for specific columns.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate incorrect subnet computation or routing logic for a given column_index.

properties.text: Validators MUST retain data column sidecars for at least MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS epochs after the block slot. During the retention period, validators MUST serve sidecars when requested by peers.

reachability.notes: An attacker could exploit premature sidecar deletion to reduce data availability below the recovery threshold.

properties.severity_justification: Premature sidecar deletion reduces data availability. If enough validators delete early, data recovery becomes impossible for affected blocks.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a scenario where sidecars are deleted before the retention period expires.

properties.text: Custody requirement computation (SG-001 get_validators_custody_requirement) MUST produce a value in [VALIDATOR_CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT, NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS]. For all validators, the custody requirement MUST be at least VALIDATOR_CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT regardless of effective_balance.

reachability.notes: The custody requirement depends on the beacon state. A forked or stale state would produce incorrect custody assignments, but the state itself comes from the consensus layer.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect custody assignments could cause some data columns to have insufficient coverage, but the minimum floor provides a safety margin.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires consensus-layer state manipulation, which is out of scope for execution-layer bounty.

properties.text: During sidecar construction (SG-002 cells_and_kzg_proofs_construction), proof slicing MUST be correctly aligned with cells: for blob i, the proofs slice MUST be proofs[i * CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB : (i+1) * CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB] and each proof[j] MUST correspond to cell[j].

reachability.notes: Proof slicing is an internal operation. Misalignment would produce sidecars that fail verification at receiving peers, effectively causing a self-DoS.

properties.severity_justification: Misaligned proof-cell pairings would cause all sidecars from the affected validator to fail verification, preventing data propagation for that blob.

properties.text: The Merkle inclusion proof computed in get_data_column_sidecars_from_block (SG-004) MUST correctly target the blob_kzg_commitments field at its generalized index in the BeaconBlockBody SSZ tree. The proof MUST be verifiable by any node with access to the block root.

reachability.notes: An incorrect generalized index would produce Merkle proofs that fail verification at all receiving peers.

properties.severity_justification: Invalid Merkle proofs would cause all data column sidecars to be rejected by peers, preventing data propagation and causing data availability failures.

properties.text: A batch verification request with an excessively large number of (commitment, cell, proof) tuples MUST be bounded by a maximum batch size. Batch sizes exceeding the maximum MUST be rejected before the pairing computation begins.

reachability.notes: An adversary could submit extremely large batches for verification, causing expensive multi-scalar multiplication and pairing operations that exhaust CPU and memory.

properties.severity_justification: Unbounded batch size allows resource exhaustion attacks that can crash or stall the node, causing denial of service.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a batch size that causes measurable resource exhaustion (memory or CPU) beyond normal operation.

properties.text: Recovery operations (SG-023, SG-024) MUST be rate-limited. A single peer MUST NOT be able to trigger unbounded recovery operations. Nodes MUST prioritize recovery for blocks on the canonical chain over recovery for non-canonical branches.

reachability.notes: Recovery involves multiple FFTs and polynomial operations. An adversary could trigger many recovery operations with minimum cell counts to maximize computational cost.

properties.severity_justification: Unbounded recovery triggers can cause CPU exhaustion. The minimum 50% cell requirement already limits cost per recovery, but repeated triggers can accumulate.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a sequence of recovery requests that causes measurable performance degradation.

properties.text: Sidecar request handling (SG-007) MUST NOT reveal custody group membership beyond what is inherently revealed by serving the requested columns. Response timing MUST NOT vary based on whether a column is in the validator's custody.

reachability.notes: An adversary could probe which columns a validator serves to infer custody group membership, enabling targeted data withholding attacks.

properties.severity_justification: Custody group inference enables targeted attacks against specific validators' data responsibilities, but does not directly compromise data availability.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a probing technique that reliably identifies custody group membership via timing or response patterns.

properties.text: decode_receipt (SG-002 blocks.py) MUST reject any Bytes receipt whose first byte is not in {1, 2, 3, 4}. The assertion receipt[0] in (1, 2, 3, 4) MUST be enforced before RLP decoding proceeds.

reachability.notes: A malicious P2P peer sends an encoded receipt with an invalid type prefix byte. If the assertion is bypassed or missing, the RLP decoder could process arbitrary malformed data.

properties.severity_justification: An unrecognized type prefix reaching the RLP decoder could cause crashes, incorrect receipt parsing, or consensus splits between clients with different error handling.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a malformed receipt that bypasses the type prefix assertion and causes incorrect behavior.

properties.text: encode_receipt (SG-001 blocks.py) MUST produce a type-prefixed encoding where the prefix byte is injective: 0x01 for AccessListTransaction, 0x02 for FeeMarketTransaction, 0x03 for BlobTransaction, 0x04 for SetCodeTransaction. LegacyTransaction receipts MUST NOT have any type prefix. No two different transaction types MUST produce the same prefix byte.

reachability.notes: If two transaction types produce the same prefix, decode_receipt would misinterpret the receipt type, causing incorrect receipt processing and potential consensus splits.

properties.severity_justification: A type prefix collision would cause all nodes to misparse receipts for one of the colliding types, leading to a network-wide consensus split.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a transaction type whose receipt encoding produces a prefix byte that collides with another type.

properties.text: encode_receipt MUST handle all transaction types exhaustively. If a new transaction type is introduced without updating encode_receipt, the function MUST NOT silently fall through to the LegacyTransaction encoding path. An unrecognized transaction type MUST cause an explicit error.

reachability.notes: This is a development-time safety property. If violated during a fork upgrade, receipts for the new type would be silently encoded as legacy, causing consensus splits.

properties.severity_justification: Silent fall-through encoding produces incorrect receipt hashes, causing consensus failure network-wide when a new transaction type is activated.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: This is a fork-upgrade safety concern, not a runtime exploit.

properties.text: decode_receipt MUST strip the type prefix byte before passing the remaining bytes to the RLP decoder. For a Bytes receipt with prefix p, rlp.decode_to(Receipt, receipt[1:]) MUST be called, NOT rlp.decode_to(Receipt, receipt). The prefix byte MUST NOT be included in the RLP payload.

reachability.notes: If the prefix byte is not stripped, the RLP decoder would attempt to parse a byte that is not part of the RLP payload, causing incorrect deserialization or crashes.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect prefix stripping would cause every typed receipt to be decoded incorrectly, leading to consensus failure for all post-EIP-2718 receipts.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a receipt where incorrect prefix handling causes RLP decode failure or incorrect field values.

properties.text: The RLP encoding produced by encode_receipt and consumed by decode_receipt MUST be a round-trip identity: for all valid (tx, receipt) pairs, decode_receipt(encode_receipt(tx, receipt)) == receipt.

reachability.notes: If encode/decode are not inverses, different clients may compute different receipt_root values for the same block, causing a consensus split.

properties.severity_justification: A round-trip failure would cause different clients to compute different receipt roots for the same block, leading to a network-wide consensus split.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a receipt whose encoded form does not decode back to the original receipt.

properties.text: parse_deposit_requests MUST filter deposit logs using a two-layer authentication: (1) log.address == DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS and (2) log.topics[0] == DEPOSIT_EVENT_SIGNATURE_HASH. Logs from any other address or with a different topic[0] MUST be excluded from deposit request extraction.

reachability.notes: A malicious contract could emit logs mimicking the deposit event signature. Without the address check, spoofed deposit events could inject unauthorized deposits.

properties.severity_justification: Accepting spoofed deposit events would allow unauthorized validator deposits, potentially corrupting the consensus validator set.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a contract that emits logs accepted as deposit events by parse_deposit_requests.

properties.text: extract_deposit_data MUST validate that deposit event data has exactly 576 bytes total length, with correct offsets and sizes for all five fields (pubkey: 48 bytes, withdrawal_credentials: 32 bytes, amount: 8 bytes, signature: 96 bytes, index: 8 bytes). Any deviation MUST raise InvalidBlock.

reachability.notes: An attacker deploying a malicious contract at the deposit address (impossible due to CREATE2 determinism) or exploiting a vulnerability in the deposit contract could emit malformed deposit data.

properties.severity_justification: Malformed deposit data that bypasses validation could corrupt the deposit request pipeline, injecting invalid BLS keys or amounts into the consensus layer.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate deposit event data that bypasses extract_deposit_data validation.

properties.text: compute_requests_hash MUST produce a deterministic SHA-256 hash over all request types in the correct order. The double-hashing construction (SHA-256 of individual requests, then SHA-256 of concatenated hashes) MUST provide domain separation between request types.

reachability.notes: If requests_hash is non-deterministic or ordering-dependent in an unspecified way, different clients could produce different hashes for the same set of requests.

properties.severity_justification: A non-deterministic requests_hash would cause consensus failure between clients that process the same block differently.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate two valid orderings of the same requests producing different hashes.

properties.text: Deposit request ordering MUST be deterministic and MUST follow the canonical receipt processing order defined by block_output.receipt_keys. For a given block, all execution clients MUST produce the identical sequence of deposit_requests bytes.

reachability.notes: A malicious block builder could manipulate receipt ordering. However, receipt_keys ordering is committed via the receipts_root in the block header.

properties.severity_justification: Non-deterministic deposit ordering would cause consensus splits between clients that process deposits in different orders.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a block where different receipt processing orders produce different deposit request sequences.

properties.text: trie_get MUST return a valid (non-None) receipt for every key in block_output.receipt_keys. If trie_get returns None for any receipt key, the assertion MUST halt processing immediately rather than silently skipping the receipt.

reachability.notes: A block builder could construct a block whose receipt_keys reference keys not present in the receipts_trie, causing the assertion to fail and the client to crash.

properties.severity_justification: A crafted block with missing trie entries would crash all clients processing it via the assertion failure, causing network-wide DoS.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a block where receipt_keys contains a key not present in the receipts trie.

properties.text: EIP-7702 Authorization tuple validation MUST verify: (1) ECDSA signature (y_parity, r, s) recovery succeeds and matches the claimed authorizer, (2) chain_id matches the current chain or is 0 (wildcard), (3) nonce matches the current nonce of the authorizing account. All three checks MUST pass before the authorization is acted upon.

reachability.notes: An attacker could submit a SetCodeTransaction with forged or replayed Authorization tuples. Without all three validation checks, unauthorized code delegation is possible.

properties.severity_justification: Bypassing Authorization validation would allow an attacker to delegate arbitrary code to any EOA without the account holder's consent, enabling full account takeover.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate an Authorization tuple that passes validation without the legitimate account holder's signature.

properties.text: encode_account MUST produce a canonical RLP encoding of the tuple (nonce, balance, storage_root, code_hash) in exactly this field order. The encoding MUST be deterministic: the same (nonce, balance, storage_root, code_hash) inputs MUST always produce the identical byte sequence.

reachability.notes: Account encoding is internal. Non-deterministic encoding would cause state trie divergence between clients.

properties.severity_justification: Non-deterministic account encoding would cause state root divergence between clients, leading to consensus split.

properties.text: Transaction sender recovery MUST use SECP256K1 ECDSA signature recovery from the (v/y_parity, r, s) components. Each transaction type MUST have its own signing hash function to prevent cross-type signature replay. The recovered sender address MUST be unique to the signer's private key.

reachability.notes: A malicious actor submits a transaction claiming to be from a different sender. The ECDSA signature binds the transaction payload to the sender's private key.

properties.severity_justification: Sender spoofing would allow an attacker to execute transactions as any account, enabling fund theft.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a transaction accepted with a sender address different from the actual signer.

properties.text: The bloom filter bytearray MUST be exactly 256 bytes (2048 bits) at all times during add_to_bloom operations. bit_to_set MUST always be in [0, 2047] due to the 0x07FF mask. byte_index (= (0x07FF - bit_to_set) // 8) MUST always be in [0, 255].

reachability.notes: The bloom filter processes log addresses and topics from executed transactions. Attacker-controlled contract code can emit logs with arbitrary addresses and topics that are hashed by add_to_bloom.

properties.severity_justification: An out-of-bounds byte_index would cause a runtime crash (DoS) or memory corruption, but the 0x07FF mask provides strong bounds enforcement.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a bloom entry that produces a byte_index outside [0, 255] despite the mask.

properties.text: add_to_bloom MUST set exactly 3 bits per bloom entry, using byte indices derived from hashed[0:2], hashed[2:4], and hashed[4:6]. The loop MUST iterate exactly 3 times with indices (0, 2, 4).

reachability.notes: If the loop iterates a different number of times, the bloom filter would set the wrong number of bits, causing false negatives or false positives in log queries.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect bit count per entry would cause bloom filter mismatches between clients, leading to consensus splits on receipt_root computation.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a bloom filter computation that sets a number of bits other than 3 per entry.

properties.text: logs_bloom (SG-002 bloom.py) MUST initialize the bloom bytearray to 256 zero bytes before processing any logs. Every log address MUST be added to the bloom exactly once. Every topic of every log MUST be added to the bloom exactly once. The returned Bloom MUST be constructed from the fully processed bytearray.

reachability.notes: Attacker-controlled contracts emit logs that are processed by logs_bloom. Missing or duplicate processing of addresses/topics would produce incorrect bloom filters.

properties.severity_justification: An incorrect bloom filter would cause the receipt_root to differ between correct and incorrect implementations, causing a consensus split.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a set of logs where logs_bloom produces an incorrect bloom filter.

properties.text: The Header data structure MUST be immutable after construction (slotted_freezable). All 21 fields MUST be set during construction. Post-construction, no field MUST be modifiable. In PoS forks, difficulty MUST be 0, nonce MUST be zero-bytes, and ommers_hash MUST be EMPTY_OMMER_HASH.

reachability.notes: A malicious block proposer could submit a block with non-zero difficulty or nonce. The validator must reject such blocks.

properties.severity_justification: Accepting a header with non-zero difficulty in PoS would indicate a validation bypass. While unlikely to directly cause consensus failure, it represents a fundamental validation gap.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a block with non-zero difficulty or nonce accepted by the validation pipeline in a PoS fork.

properties.text: The Block data structure MUST have an empty ommers tuple in PoS forks. ommers MUST be Tuple[Header, ...] with length 0. Any block with non-empty ommers MUST be rejected.

reachability.notes: A malicious proposer could include ommer headers in a post-merge block. If accepted, this would violate PoS consensus rules.

properties.severity_justification: Accepting non-empty ommers post-merge would indicate a validation gap but is unlikely to be exploitable beyond causing client inconsistencies.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a post-merge block with non-empty ommers accepted by the validation pipeline.

properties.text: Withdrawal objects MUST be immutable after construction. All four fields (index, validator_index, address, amount) MUST be set. The execution layer MUST process withdrawal amounts exactly as specified by the consensus layer without modification.

reachability.notes: Fabricated withdrawal instructions at the Engine API boundary could mint unauthorized ETH. JWT authentication is the primary defense.

properties.severity_justification: Accepting fabricated withdrawals would cause unauthorized ETH minting on the execution layer, directly impacting fund security.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a withdrawal injection that bypasses Engine API authentication.

properties.text: The Receipt data structure MUST be immutable after construction. The bloom field MUST be consistent with the logs field: logs_bloom(receipt.logs) MUST equal receipt.bloom. cumulative_gas_used MUST be monotonically non-decreasing within a block.

reachability.notes: Receipt construction is internal. An inconsistent bloom would cause receipt_root divergence between implementations.

properties.severity_justification: Inconsistent bloom-to-logs relationship would cause receipt root mismatches between clients, leading to consensus split.

properties.text: Log objects MUST be immutable after construction. The topics tuple MUST have at most 4 elements (enforced by LOG0-LOG4 opcodes). The address MUST be a valid 20-byte Address.

reachability.notes: Attacker-controlled contract code emits logs. The EVM enforces the topic limit at the opcode level. If the limit is not enforced, a log with >4 topics would cause bloom filter processing to differ between correct and incorrect implementations.

properties.severity_justification: A log with >4 topics would indicate an EVM constraint violation. The impact is limited to bloom filter miscalculation and potential consensus divergence.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a log with >4 topics reaching the bloom filter pipeline.

properties.text: Withdrawal data from the consensus layer MUST be authenticated via the Engine API JWT mechanism. The parent_beacon_block_root field MUST provide a cryptographic anchor to the beacon chain state. Withdrawals not authorized by the beacon chain MUST be rejected.

reachability.notes: An attacker at the Engine API boundary could inject fabricated withdrawal instructions. JWT authentication and beacon root verification are the primary defenses.

properties.severity_justification: Unauthorized withdrawal injection would mint ETH on the execution layer without consensus authorization, directly causing fund loss.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate withdrawal injection bypassing Engine API authentication.

properties.text: Block header timestamp MUST be strictly greater than the parent block's timestamp. Block number MUST equal parent_number + 1. base_fee_per_gas MUST follow EIP-1559 adjustment rules. blob_gas_used and excess_blob_gas MUST follow EIP-4844 rules.

reachability.notes: A malicious block proposer could submit blocks with manipulated timestamps or fees to gain MEV advantages or cause consensus issues.

properties.severity_justification: Accepting invalid timestamps or fee calculations would violate consensus rules, potentially enabling MEV exploitation or consensus splits.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a block with invalid header fields accepted by the validation pipeline.

properties.text: The RLP codec MUST enforce canonical encoding: no leading zeros in integer encodings, shortest-form encoding for all elements. encode_receipt and decode_receipt MUST use the same RLP implementation. Different RLP implementations MUST produce identical byte sequences for the same input.

reachability.notes: A malicious peer could send non-canonical RLP encodings to test whether the receiving client accepts them. Acceptance of non-canonical encodings could cause state divergence.

properties.severity_justification: Non-canonical RLP encoding acceptance would cause receipt_root/state_root divergence between clients, leading to consensus split.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a non-canonical RLP encoding accepted by one client implementation but rejected by another.

properties.text: keccak256 output for bloom filter construction MUST be at least 6 bytes long to support 3 pairs of 2-byte reads at indices (0,1), (2,3), (4,5). The keccak256 implementation MUST be collision-resistant and deterministic.

reachability.notes: keccak256 always produces 32 bytes of output, so the 6-byte minimum is always satisfied. This property verifies the hash function's output length guarantee.

properties.severity_justification: keccak256 is well-established to produce 32-byte outputs. This property is primarily a sanity check.

properties.text: ECDSA signature components (v/y_parity, r, s) in transactions and Authorization tuples MUST be validated for correct ranges before signature recovery. r and s MUST be in [1, SECP256K1_ORDER - 1]. y_parity MUST be 0 or 1.

reachability.notes: Attacker submits a transaction with out-of-range r or s values. Without range validation, signature recovery could produce unexpected results.

properties.severity_justification: Out-of-range signature components could cause signature recovery to behave unpredictably across different ECDSA implementations, potentially allowing signature forgery or causing consensus splits.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate an out-of-range signature component that causes incorrect sender recovery.

properties.text: The decode_receipt function MUST safely handle extremely large or deeply nested RLP payloads from untrusted peers without causing memory exhaustion or stack overflow. Maximum element sizes and nesting depth MUST be enforced by the RLP decoder.

reachability.notes: A malicious P2P peer sends crafted RLP payloads designed to exhaust memory or cause stack overflow during decoding.

properties.severity_justification: Memory exhaustion or stack overflow in the RLP decoder would crash the node, causing denial of service.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a crafted RLP payload that causes measurable resource exhaustion during decode_receipt processing.

properties.text: bytes_to_bls_field and bls_field_to_bytes MUST be correct inverse operations for all valid BLS12-381 scalar field elements. For all valid field elements f, bytes_to_bls_field(bls_field_to_bytes(f)) == f. For all valid byte sequences b (representing values < BLS_MODULUS), bls_field_to_bytes(bytes_to_bls_field(b)) == b.

reachability.notes: Blob data enters via transactions and is deserialized into field elements. If serialization is not a round-trip identity, data corruption occurs.

properties.severity_justification: Non-invertible field element serialization would corrupt blob data during encoding/decoding cycles, breaking data availability guarantees for affected blobs.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a field element value where the round-trip serialization produces a different value.
